title: Gateway auth-metadata race caused soft-429 cascade; mitigation and long-term fixes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a regional load surge on 2026-03-01 (internal model-eval traffic and external customer burst), the API gateway began returning elevated soft 429 responses for a subset of authenticated requests. The pattern was unusual: requests with valid tokens were intermittently counted against a shared fallback quota key instead of the correct org/client key, causing one quota partition to hit its window limit and cascade into retries and additional pressure on adjacent partitions. The window of degraded service lasted ~12 minutes across three regions with intermittent partial recoveries.

Timeline (high level):
- 09:11 UTC: traffic spike begins after nightly eval ramp + customer job; first anomalies in per-token dashboards.
- 09:13 UTC: automated alert for rising 429 rate in gateway-east-1; SRE page and eng on-call engaged.
- 09:15 UTC: investigation shows increased counts attributed to a single quota key ("fallback-anon-v2") while origin tokens still valid.
- 09:16 UTC: deployed temporary mitigation: disable auth-metadata async refresh path (force synchronous enrich) and increase local per-shard temporary soft limit.
- 09:23 UTC: 429s decline as caches warm and enforcer shards rebalance.
- 09:35 UTC: post-incident monitoring continues; elevated error-rate subsides to baseline by 09:43 UTC.

Root cause (summary):
Two interacting issues led to misattribution of quota counts:
1) Auth metadata refresh race: the gateway enriched incoming requests with auth metadata (org_id, token_type, priority) using a best-effort async refresh path. Under latency for the metadata service, requests occasionally flowed through before enrichment completed. The enrichment code used a non-atomic update to request-scoped metadata and a temporary sentinel value when enrichment was incomplete.
2) Quota-key normalization fallback: when enrichment was missing, the quota normalization function fell back to a shared anonymous key ("fallback-anon-v2") instead of deferring or using a provisional per-token key. This caused many distinct clients to be counted against the same partition for the quota window.
Neither issue alone would have caused the cascade at production scale, but together they concentrated counts and triggered cross-shard hot spots. Existing rate-limiter retries and client backoffs amplified the impact.

Impact: 
- Duration: ~12 minutes of increased 429 rate with residual tracing for 1 hour.
- Scope: 3 regions (east, central, west), ~13% of traffic from affected customers experienced soft 429s at peak.
- Customers: 7 paying customers reported degraded throughput; two support tickets escalated to SEs.
- Operational: on-call SRE and gateway team logged ~2.5 hours of follow-up work (mitigation, investigation, and follow-ups).

Immediate mitigations applied during the incident: 
- Forced synchronous metadata enrich for incoming auth tokens to prevent processing before enrichment completes (rollback-safe flagged deploy).
- Temporarily increased local shard soft limits and enabled emergency shard rebalancing to spread the misattributed load.
- Tuned gateway retry headers (Retry-After) and posted advisory to internal client SDKs to throttle aggressive clients during the window.

Longer-term remediation and action items are below (owner + due date included). Relevant logs, dashboards and PRs are linked in the links section.
action_items: ENG-48673-A1: Make auth metadata enrichment atomic at request scope (use immutable RequestContext snapshot). Owner: Diego Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-14.

ENG-48673-A2: Change quota-key normalization to never map missing metadata to global anonymous bucket; instead return a provisional per-token bucket and mark for reconciliation. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-21.
ENG-48673-A3: Add unit + integration tests for enrichment race and fallback behavior in gateway CI; include synthetic delay injection. Owner: Test Infra (Liam O'Connor). Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-18.
ENG-48673-A4: Enhance observability: create a derived metric for 'quota key churn' and an alert when >2% of requests use fallback keys. Owner: SRE (Ruth Kim). Due: 2026-03-10.
ENG-48673-A5: Run canary load test that simulates enrichment latency across all regions to ensure no hot-shard behavior. Owner: Performance Team (Anika Patel). Due: 2026-03-25.
ENG-48673-A6: Update gateway runbook with explicit guidance for metadata races, emergency config toggles, and recommended retry header values. Owner: Oncall Lead (Mason Reed). Due: 2026-03-08.
ENG-48673-A7: Implement a short-term cheat: when enrichment latency detected, garbage-collect old sentinel mappings within 1s to avoid persistent grouping. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-09.
ENG-48673-A8: Post-deploy monitoring window: 72-hour elevated telemetry collection after changes; SRE to run regression checks and sign-off. Owner: SRE (Ruth Kim). Due: 2026-04-01.
ENG-48673-A9: Identify customers impacted and coordinate customer-facing postmortem and credits with CS. Owner: Solutions Eng (Hannah Lee). Due: 2026-03-12.
ENG-48673-A10: Audit other codepaths that use sentinel fallback values in request processing and standardize defensive patterns. Owner: Platform Safety (Marco Silva). Due: 2026-03-28.
